How It Works: Industry-standard platform. Create speaker profile, get discovered by bureaus and event planners. Also serves as back-end CRM for many agencies.
Commission: Free basic profile; Premium $399/year for enhanced visibility + tools
Requirements: Professional bio, headshot, demo video, topic list
Notes: MUST-HAVE. Many bureaus use eSpeakers as their backend. Being listed here means you show up in bureau searches. Priority #1.

How It Works: Create free profile, get discovered by event planners searching for speakers. SEO-friendly profiles rank well in Google.
Commission: Free basic; Premium €29/month for analytics + featured placement
Notes: Great SEO. Profiles often rank on page 1 of Google for '[topic] speaker' searches. Free to start.

How It Works: Respond to conference Calls for Papers (CFPs). Conferences post speaker requests, speakers apply. Used by most tech conferences.
Notes: Primary CFP platform for tech conferences. Create profile and actively monitor for relevant CFPs. MUST-HAVE for conference circuit.

How It Works: Speakers bureau with online presence. Submit to be considered for their roster. They actively market speakers to corporate clients.
Requirements: Professional credentials, demo video, speaking history
Notes: Santa Barbara-based. Good for tech/innovation speakers. Active roster curation.

How It Works: General events marketplace with corporate speaker category. Create profile, get inbound leads from event planners.
Commission: Free to browse; Pro membership $10-30/month for direct leads
Notes: More event-focused but has growing corporate speaker segment. Good for regional/smaller gigs.

How It Works: Matching service connecting speakers with event planners. Create profile, get matched with opportunities.
Commission: Free basic; Premium for enhanced visibility ($20/month)
Notes: Good for inbound leads. Not as well-known but steady flow of event planners.

How It Works: Speaker portfolio site. Upload slides, videos, and details from past talks. Not a booking platform — a showcase.
Notes: Great for building an online speaker portfolio. Embed on personal website. SEO benefits.

How It Works: Speaker directory and booking platform. Create profile, set rates, get booked directly.
Notes: Growing platform. Good for direct bookings without bureau intermediary.

How It Works: Enable 'Keynote Speaker' or 'Public Speaker' in LinkedIn Services section. Event planners search LinkedIn for speakers.
Requirements: Active LinkedIn profile with speaking-related content
Notes: Free and underutilized. Many event planners search LinkedIn first. Add 'Keynote Speaker' to services. Priority #2.

How It Works: Speaker directory and booking service. List profile, receive direct inquiries from event planners.
Notes: Growing marketplace. Good for supplemental inbound leads.

How It Works: Speaker directory focused on professional/business speakers. Good for SEO and discovery.
Notes: Directory-style. Helps with search engine visibility.

How It Works: Hybrid bureau/marketplace. Both actively market speakers and allow event planners to search/book directly.
Notes: Large platform. Good visibility across price ranges.

How It Works: Search-focused platform where event planners find speakers by topic, location, fee range.
Notes: Good for inbound discovery.

How It Works: Direct booking platform. Create profile, set rates, receive booking inquiries.
Notes: Straightforward booking service.

How It Works: Online speaker booking platform. Create profile, get booked for corporate and conference events.
Notes: Growing platform. Responsive to applications.

How It Works: Video-first speaker platform. Upload talk recordings, get discovered by event planners who want to see you speak before booking.
Notes: Video-first discovery. Great if you have strong stage footage.

How It Works: NSA membership includes listing in their speaker directory. Event planners search for NSA-certified speakers.
Notes: Professional credibility. CSP (Certified Speaking Professional) designation is gold standard. Worth pursuing.

How It Works: Not a booking platform, but Toastmasters chapters often hire speakers for events, and members become referral sources.
Commission: Free (attend as guest; membership ~$50/6months if desired)
Requirements: Willingness to engage with local chapters
Notes: Toastmasters members = event planners, HR people, executives. Great referral network.

How It Works: Not a marketplace — it's a CRM and business tool specifically built for professional speakers. Manage leads, contracts, follow-ups.
Notes: Essential business tool once you're doing 10+ talks/year. Tracks leads, manages contracts, invoicing.

How It Works: European speaker marketplace. Create profile, get discovered by European event planners.
Notes: Gateway to European market. Good for expanding beyond US.

How It Works: UK speaker marketplace. Create profile, get booked for UK/European events.
Notes: UK market access.

How It Works: Platform matching speakers with corporate off-sites and leadership events. Curated speaker roster.
Notes: Corporate-focused. Good for corporate retreat/off-site bookings.
